object_description: clearly cut three-storey block filling the perimeter around a central atrium
design_condition: the block fills the project perimeter and forms an adequate counterpart to the existing buildings, articulating the space between them as an open square with facing main entrances

positive: Together with a regularly structured facade, an adequate counterpart to the existing buildings is created
The intermediate space is articulated as an open square linking the two institutions
The main entrance is logically located at street level and easy to find
The garage exit is simply positioned and the school route can stay straight and unobstructed
The spacious, well-proportioned central atrium aids orientation and lights the central zone
Wide bridges on the upper floors form high-quality common areas that can be used in different ways
The facade construction is pragmatically designed and well thought out in structure and material
The architectural expression is appropriate and sympathetic to the situation and significance of the building
Varied room depth creates appropriately deep rooms for classrooms and smaller rooms for offices
Implementation of the room programme and the distribution of uses are largely logical
Landscaping is used with restraint and adapted to the needs of the users
Construction, materials and detailing show an economical approach to design
A high degree of urban planning and architectural quality is attested
negative: The entrance to the building lacks conciseness and architectural sharpness
The findability and architectural formulation of the vertical circulation is all too understated
The longitudinal, statically effective corridor walls need review for structure and flexibility of use
Space requirements are not met, particularly in the utility area
Building costs are in the upper range
The facade structure without a plinth takes little account of the topographical slope
